fixes.explanation: In verse 9 God speaks to Jeroboam through Ahijah: "You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me…" Molten images are idols cast from metal. So "other gods and metal idols" is exactly what God names. Jeroboam made them, and God says they were to provoke Him.

Ships sound like something a big kingdom would build, but this passage never mentions them. In verse 9 God says Jeroboam made "…other gods and molten images…" Those are the things He names in His message. Trading ships don't show up anywhere in it.

A cedar palace sounds like something a king would build, but verse 9 says no such thing. God says Jeroboam made "…other gods and molten images…" Those are the things He names. A palace isn't in His message at all.

Ahijah says it in verse 12: "When your feet enter the city, the child will die." I think this is the hardest line in the whole passage. She hears it in Shiloh, and then she has to go home. Verse 17 says it happened as she stepped over the threshold of the house.

That's not what Ahijah says. In verse 12 he first tells her to get up and go home. Then he says the child will die when her feet enter the city. So it comes after she leaves Shiloh, not before. I think that's a hard thing to be told.

No number of days is given. Ahijah ties it to her feet entering the city in verse 12: "When your feet enter the city, the child will die." Verse 17 shows it happening as she steps over the threshold of the house. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

Ahijah tells her in verse 13 that this boy is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will receive a proper burial, "because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam." Out of a whole house, one boy is singled out. I think that's a quiet kindness tucked inside a hard message.

The text never says Abijah was the firstborn, so that isn't the reason it gives. In verse 13 Ahijah says it's "because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam." The reason is what the LORD found in him. Nothing is said about where he stood in the family.

His mother is the one who makes the trip, and nothing in the text says Abijah asked anyone for anything. In verse 13 Ahijah gives the reason: "because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam." The reason is what the LORD found in him. It isn't something the boy asked for.

True. In verse 14 Ahijah says the LORD "…will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam." The king is raised up for the LORD Himself. That matches verse 10, where the house of Jeroboam was already named in the disaster.

Ahijah says it will. In verse 14 he says the LORD "…will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam." The king is raised up for the LORD Himself. Verse 10 had already named the house of Jeroboam in the disaster.
There's no lamp in this message, friend. In verse 15 Ahijah says the LORD will strike Israel "…as a reed is shaken in the water." The picture is a reed and water. Nothing about a lamp or the night.

No broken jar in this message. In verse 15 Ahijah says the LORD will strike Israel "…as a reed is shaken in the water." It's a reed in water, not a jar on the ground. Nothing gets smashed in that picture.

In verse 15 Ahijah says the LORD will uproot Israel "…from this good land that He gave their fathers…" The land was a gift to those who came before them. To be uprooted from a gift is a heavy thing, I think.

Prophets get lots of lines in this chapter, since one is doing the talking. But in verse 15 Ahijah says the land is the one "…that He gave their fathers…" The word there is fathers, not prophets. The land came to them first, and the message is about Israel being uprooted from it.
No priests in this message. In verse 15 Ahijah says the land is the one "…that He gave their fathers…" The land was given to the fathers. The message is about Israel being uprooted from it.

Ahijah says in verse 16 that God will give Israel over "…on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit." That's two things: what Jeroboam did and what he led Israel into. Verse 15 names the Asherah poles Israel made, provoking the LORD to anger.

Solomon is a name from earlier in the story, and he's gone by now. 1 Kings 11:43 says he rested with his fathers and Rehoboam reigned in his place. Ahijah's words in verse 16 are about "the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit."

True. Verse 17 says, "…as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died." Ahijah had told her the child would die when her feet entered the city (1 Kings 14:12). It's a heavy moment, friend.
Verse 20 says, "…his son Nadab reigned in his place." Jeroboam's reign lasted twenty-two years, and then he rested with his fathers. After that the throne goes to Nadab.
He does greet her that way. Verse 6 has Ahijah say, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised?" He knew who she was as soon as he heard her. I'd ask for a refund on that costume.

Ahijah says it in his own words: "…I have been sent to you with bad news." (1 Kings 14:6). She came for an answer about her son, and he doesn't dress it up. I think that's a heavy thing to hear at a door.
No peace news here, friend. In verse 6 Ahijah says, "…I have been sent to you with bad news." The rest of the passage shows how heavy it is. It's a hard word to bring about her son.

Victory would be a nice thing to hear at a door, but that's not what he brings. In verse 6 Ahijah says he has been sent with "bad news." Nothing in this scene is a victory lap. It's a heavy part of the story, friend.

In verse 8 God speaks through Ahijah, and He says David "kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes." That's the measure God holds up. It's about David's heart following Him. Heart first, friend, always.

David did bring up the ark of God to the City of David (2 Samuel 6:12), but that's not Shiloh, and it isn't what God names here. Verse 8 points to David keeping God's commandments and following Him with all his heart. Shiloh is where Ahijah is in this story, but the ark isn't part of God's message.

It's actually true. In verse 9 God says to Jeroboam through Ahijah, "You have done more evil than all who came before you." That's a heavy line, friend. The verse goes right on to name other gods and molten images.
God says to Jeroboam through Ahijah, "I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel…" (1 Kings 14:10). That's a heavy line, friend. I think this one hurts.

Verse 8 does mention the house of David, as the one the kingdom was torn from. But in verse 10 God says He will cut off every male belonging to Jeroboam. Nothing there is about serving anybody. I think it's a hard sentence.
